You are an adversarial deep-tech investor. MARKET skeptic: is the customer and budget real? Would anyone pay in the next 18 months? Attack TAM inflation.
Default to skepticism; score 1-10 where 7+ means you would actually take a meeting. Thesis:
{
  "name": "OpenBeam (merchant OCI-MSA optical engine, non-TSMC)",
  "one_liner": "The multi-source UCIe-fronted optical engine the hyperscalers just standardized for — built on GlobalFoundries/Tower instead of TSMC, sold to everyone who isn't NVIDIA.",
  "wedge": "An OCI-MSA-compliant optical chiplet (UCIe electrical side, parallel CWDM WDM optical side, targeting the standard's path to 3.2Tb/s per link) fabbed on GF Fotonix (monolithic CMOS+photonics, proven with Lightmatter/Ayar) or Tower/OpenLight (integrated lasers), sold to custom-XPU programs — hyperscaler ASIC teams (Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft via Alchip/Broadcom-custom/Marvell-rivals) and AMD-ecosystem players who need optical scale-up but refuse single-vendor lock-in on Ayar Labs or a Marvell subsidiary.",
  "why_now": "The OCI MSA (March 2026, founded by AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI) explicitly standardizes a multi-vendor optical scale-up interface — hyperscalers created it precisely because they want second and third sources. Consolidation just deleted the independents: Celestial→Marvell, Nubis→Ciena, DustPhotonics→Credo, Enosemi→AMD. Ayar Labs is the only scaled independent chiplet vendor left, and it just joined NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion orbit — making a neutral alternative more valuable, not less. GF is hungry for anchor photonics customers post-AMF acquisition and will co-invest in enablement.",
  "market": "Optical scale-up is the genuinely enormous prize: CPO $8-10B by 2030, with the scale-up tier (GPU-to-GPU/memory) called 'a new market' by LightCounting and validated by Celestial's $3.25B exit and Marvell's claimed ~$10B addressable. A merchant engine vendor winning 2-3 hyperscaler custom-silicon sockets ships millions of chiplets: $500M-1B+ revenue potential by 2030-2032. This is the biggest TAM of any thesis here — and the hardest to reach.",
  "competition": "Savage, and mostly better-funded: Ayar Labs ($870M raised, NVIDIA/AMD/Intel all invested, NVLink Fusion member, 5-year head start); Marvell/Celestial (owns the AWS-adjacent custom-XPU channel); Broadcom (will offer OCI engines alongside its custom-ASIC business); Lightmatter (interposer approach, ~$12.5B IPO war chest); Intel's OCI chiplet program; plus TSMC COUPE gravitationally pulling the biggest customers to its ecosystem. You win only on the specific vector of neutrality + non-TSMC supply + OCI-native design — and only if hyperscalers' multi-sourcing rhetoric converts to purchase orders for a startup.",
  "moat": "Thin until a design win, then extremely thick: a socket in a hyperscaler XPU program is a 3-5 year committed ramp with co-developed test/packaging flows. Pre-win, the defensible assets are microring/WDM design IP that hits OCI specs on GF's process (nontrivial porting work others haven't done), laser-integration route via OpenLight/Tower that TSMC-ecosystem rivals lack, and the neutrality position itself.",
  "capital_intensity": "High — this is honest deep-tech fabless, not lean: $30-50M to a credible sampling chiplet (multiple full mask sets at >$500K each, 4-6 month cycles, packaging/test development, a 40+ person mixed photonics/SerDes team), $150-300M cumulative to production qualification. The Ayar fundraising history ($870M) is the realistic benchmark. Requires a strategic CVC (AMD, a hyperscaler, GF itself) by Series A or don't start.",
  "software_mvp": "This week: an OCI-MSA link-compliance and architecture-exploration toolkit — open-source models of the MSA's UCIe+WDM stack, letting XPU architects sweep engine configurations (wavelength counts, launch power vs the ~24.5dBm budget, ring tuning overhead at ~0.12nm/mW) against their bandwidth/pJ-per-bit targets. It builds relationships with the exact 10 architecture teams who will someday buy the chiplet, shapes the spec conversation, and costs nothing but engineering time.",
  "risks": [
    "Capital risk dominates: $150M+ before meaningful revenue, in a sector where crossover funding can evaporate with the AI cycle",
    "Hyperscaler multi-sourcing may in practice mean 'Ayar plus Broadcom,' never a startup — the MSA guarantees an interface, not a customer",
    "TSMC COUPE ecosystem lock: if the volume packaging flow standardizes on COUPE, GF-based engines fight uphill on cost/integration",
    "Talent war: microring DWDM + UCIe SerDes engineers are being paid NVIDIA money",
    "Timing: optical scale-up volume is 2028-2030 (Feynman-generation per SemiAnalysis); a 2026 start hits the window only with flawless execution",
    "Acquisition is the likely 'success' outcome, and post-consolidation the buyer list is short (Broadcom won't, Marvell/AMD/Credo already bought)"
  ]
}

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the OCI MSA:

## Overview

The Optical Compute Interconnect (OCI) Multi-Source Agreement (MSA) group was announced on March 12, 2026, led by founding members AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA and OpenAI.

## Purpose

This industry consortium marks a pivotal shift toward a hyperscaler-driven open ecosystem to enable the development of a multi-vendor supply chain for optical scale-up interconnects. By aligning on an open specification, the OCI MSA members are promoting a robust optical ecosystem which will ensure that the future of AI interconnects is built with a flexible, multi-vendor foundation to meet the optical interconnect needs of modern AI infrastructure.

## Technical Approach

As large language models advance toward super intelligence, traditional copper-based connectivity is reaching limitations in physical reach which are impacting AI cluster scale-up domain architectures. OCI will enable migration from copper-based to optical-based scale-up architectures, alleviating copper interconnect bottlenecks.

The OCI specification combines non-return to zero (NRZ) modulation and wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) optical technology and shifts the connectivity paradigm from a module-centric to a silicon-centric model.

## Technical Specifications

OCI GEN1 provides 4 wavelengths × 50 Gbps NRZ per direction (200 Gbps per direction), with OCI GEN2 targeting 400 Gbps per direction BiDi architecture and a maximum fiber capacity roadmap scaling toward 3.2 Tbps per fiber.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Ayar Labs and the NVLink Fusion ecosystem:

## Key Announcement

Ayar Labs announced it has joined the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem in June 2026, making its products optically and electrically compatible with NVIDIA optical and SerDes technologies.

## Optical Chiplet Innovation

Ayar claimed to have unveiled the world's first UCIe optical interconnect chiplet, with ASIC company Alchip working to develop scalable AI infrastructure based on the technology. Ayar Labs has developed optical chiplets meant to sit alongside GPUs and other processors, converting electrical signals into light only millimeters from the compute silicon.

## Benefits for Hyperscalers

This allows hyperscalers and system innovators to build optically-connected AI infrastructure around NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion platform and partner ecosystem. Ayar Labs' CPO solution is designed to address scaling limits by bringing high-bandwidth, low-latency, power-efficient connectivity to NVLink Fusion architectures, helping customers expand design headroom as bandwidth requirements grow.

## Market Context

As AI factories scale to larger GPU counts and increasingly heterogeneous architectures, data movement and power are turning into critical bottlenecks, requiring system designers to rethink how compute elements are connected, how bandwidth scales over distance, and how power is allocated across the rack.

input.rationale: The facts check out — OCI MSA is real (announced 2026-03-12, per Businesswire/Tom's Hardware) and Ayar did join NVLink Fusion (June 2026) — but the market case fails the 18-month payment test catastrophically, by the thesis's own numbers. The customer is a hyperscaler custom-XPU program that qualifies suppliers against working silicon; this startup is $30-50M and 2+ years from a sampling chiplet, so revenue in 18 months is structurally zero. Worse, 'the hyperscalers just standardized' is an overclaim: the consortium was established to CREATE a spec, not one that exists — GEN1 is a modest 4x50G NRZ (200Gb/s per direction), the 3.2Tb/s is roadmap vapor, and the spec authors include Broadcom and NVIDIA, the exact incumbents who will fill the 'multi-vendor' slots. An MSA guarantees an interface, not a purchase order — the thesis admits this in its own risks section, then ignores it. The TAM is inflated by category conflation: $8-10B CPO-by-2030 is the whole co-packaged-optics market (dominated by Broadcom/NVIDIA switch CPO and the TSMC COUPE ecosystem); the serviceable slice for a fourth-place merchant vendor behind Ayar (NVLink Fusion, $870M raised), Marvell/Celestial, and Broadcom is plausibly under $200M by 2030 — and the $500M-1B revenue claim is circular, valid only if the design wins that constitute the whole risk actually land. Buyer concentration is brutal: ~6 customers with monopsony power who have demonstrably preferred acquiring optical teams (AMD/Enosemi, Marvell/Celestial, Credo/DustPhotonics) over issuing POs to startups — note AMD buying Enosemi directly undercuts the 'AMD-ecosystem players need a merchant engine' wedge. The honest version of this thesis is 'build silicon good enough to be acquired by 2029,' which is a legitimate deep-tech bet on strategic value (Celestial exited at $3.25B pre-revenue), not a market with a paying customer. The demand direction is genuinely real and hyperscaler-pulled, which is rare, and the thesis is unusually candid — that keeps it at a 4 rather than a 2, but I would not take the meeting without a signed, paid NRE commitment from a strategic already in hand.
fatal_flaws: Zero path to revenue inside 18 months by the thesis's own capital plan ($30-50M just to a sampling chiplet, $150-300M to qualification); the only near-term money is strategic NRE/subsidy, which is not a market

The 'standard' doesn't exist yet: OCI MSA was formed March 2026 to create a spec (GEN1 only 200Gb/s per direction, NRZ), and its authors include Broadcom and NVIDIA — the startup would be building compliant silicon against a moving target written by its competitors

TAM conflation: $8-10B is total CPO including switch/transceiver CPO the startup can never touch; serviceable market for a 4th-place merchant chiplet vendor after Ayar, Marvell/Celestial, Broadcom, Intel is likely <$200M by 2030

Multi-sourcing rhetoric converts to 'Ayar plus Broadcom,' not to a startup: hyperscalers qualify second sources against proven silicon and HVM laser-reliability data a 2026 start cannot produce before the 2028-2030 window closes

Buyer base is ~6 monopsonists who have repeatedly chosen acquisition over procurement (AMD/Enosemi, Marvell/Celestial, Credo/DustPhotonics); AMD's Enosemi purchase specifically deletes the thesis's 'AMD-ecosystem customers' wedge
improvements: Reframe honestly as an acquisition-outcome bet: underwrite to a Celestial-style strategic exit at silicon-proof stage (~$50M in), not to $500M-1B merchant revenue, and structure the cap table and milestones accordingly

Make a signed, paid development contract (not an MOU) from GF, AMD, or one hyperscaler XPU team a pre-seed go/no-go gate — the thesis already concedes 'strategic CVC by Series A or don't start'; move that to day zero
Rebuild TAM bottom-up: named XPU programs x chiplets per socket x realistic ASP x plausible share for a non-incumbent, instead of quoting LightCounting's whole-category CPO number

Monetize the wedge earlier: sell OCI compliance/test IP, link-modeling tools, and GF-Fotonix reference designs as paid engagements in 2026-2027 to prove someone will actually spend budget, rather than open-sourcing the only near-term product

Get evidence that any hyperscaler has ever issued a production PO to a sub-scale optical startup (vs. investing in or acquiring one) — if no precedent exists, the entire merchant-engine premise needs a channel partner (e.g., ride inside an Alchip/Marvell-rival custom-ASIC offering)
